title: Toys R Us Set to Leave Japan After 35 Years
paragraphs: Toys R Us, the famous American toy store chain, is leaving Japan after 35 years.

On October 1, Toys R Us Asia, which is based in Hong Kong, announced that it had agreed to transfer its business in Japan to a company connected to Pan Pacific International Holdings. Pan Pacific is the parent company of Don Quijote, a popular chain of discount stores in Japan. According to Nikkei, the deal could be worth about 10 billion yen.

Toys R Us opened its first store in Japan in 1991, in Ibaraki Prefecture. Over the years, it grew to around 150 stores across the country, including Babies R Us stores. It has about 6,000 full-time and part-time workers.
The good news for workers is that the company will not simply close. Pan Pacific is expected to take over the stores and continue to employ the staff.
So why is Toys R Us leaving? The company has been losing money for many years. In fact, Toys R Us Japan reported losses for eight years in a row up to December 2025.

Experts point to several different reasons for its problems. First, Japan's birth rate has fallen a lot, so there are fewer young children to buy toys for. Second, more parents now prefer to shop online instead of visiting large stores. Third, Toys R Us faces strong competition from electronics stores such as Yodobashi Camera and Bic Camera. These stores sell toys too, and they are often in more central locations in cities.

Interestingly, Toys R Us lasted much longer in Japan than in the US, where it started. The last Toys R Us store in the US closed in 2017, but the Japanese business continued for about nine more years.
